Subject: Crosswind renewal architecture & onramp playbook

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the catch-up yesterday. As promised, attaching a draft quote and a short mutual action plan that sketches a few structured options for the renewal and ramp. High-level thinking:

- Option A: 2-year hybrid term (co-term to Nov 1 FY) with a frontloaded burst credit + staged ramp (20% Y1, 60% Y2).
- Option B: 3-year laddered term with annual true-ups and a capped overage construct.
- Governance: quarterly exercise to adjust batching/quantization profile if usage deviates >30%.

Two points you raised we flagged for legal/procurement: auto-renew preferences and the ability to true-up mid-term for burst events. We can structure both, but procurement usually prefers a soft auto-renew (notification + opt-out window) rather than hard auto-renew.

Next steps: can you confirm (1) your preferred budget owner & procurement timeline, (2) whether Nov 1 co-term works for your fiscal syncing, and (3) availability for a 30-min alignment next week?

Attachments: redwood_quote_v2.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks,
David Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Quick notes from an ops/CS perspective:

- Recommend Option A (2-year hybrid term) as primary. It balances revenue visibility with a reasonable ramp profile for the customer.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups are operationally feasible if we automate usage exports and have RBAC hooks for their finance team — avoids big surprises.
- Auto-renew language: propose "soft auto-renew" with 45-day notification and explicit opt-out; procurement likes this.
- SLA credits: propose a 5% service credit cap per quarter for sustained SLO misses (documented via our Console traces).

Also attached a short term comparison matrix I put together (term_matrix.csv) to illustrate margin sensitivity across structures.

Operational asks: we will need a committed onboarding plan for the frontloaded burst credit so CS can staff for the anticipated spike.

Kimberly Park
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

- Offer a pilot bonus: additional 5% credit if they hit integration milestone M1 within 60 days.
- Legal: request a short amendment template that enables co-terming to Nov 1 and defines the opt-out window.

Next steps I will take (today):
- Draft amendment and send to legal for a quick review (target 48 hrs).
- Update the quote PDF to reflect 10% protection and the pilot bonus.
- Confirm final deal id DL-8732 and prepare the sales deck for the 11/2 meeting.

If there are no objections I will share the updated materials and lock a 30-min slot with Olivia for 11/2 at 2:30pm PT.
